step.goal: Load context and identify infrastructure scope
step.action: Identify all services, databases, caches, queues, and external dependencies
step.output: Infrastructure scope: {{service_count}} services, {{db_count}} databases, {{external_count}} external dependencies

step.action: Map each application service to infrastructure: - Compute platform (containers, serverless, VMs) - Network placement (public, private, DMZ) - Service mesh or API gateway - Inter-service communication (REST, gRPC, events) - Load balancing configuration
Create a Mermaid diagram of the service topology

Map data requirements to infrastructure: - Primary database(s) — engine, size, replication - Cache layer(s) — engine, cluster mode, persistence - Message queue(s) — engine, partitions, consumers - Object storage — bucket structure, lifecycle rules - Search engine (if needed) — engine, index strategy

Define the deployment pipeline: - Source control branching strategy - Build stage (compile, lint, unit test) - Test stage (integration, E2E, security scan) - Deploy stage (staging, production) - Rollback mechanism - Feature flag integration (if applicable)
Create a Mermaid diagram of the CI/CD pipeline

Define all environments:
| Aspect | Development | Staging | Production | |--------|-------------|---------|------------| | Purpose | {{dev_purpose}} | {{staging_purpose}} | {{prod_purpose}} | | Scale | {{dev_scale}} | {{staging_scale}} | {{prod_scale}} | | Data | {{dev_data}} | {{staging_data}} | {{prod_data}} | | Access | {{dev_access}} | {{staging_access}} | {{prod_access}} |
Specify IaC approach: - Tool (Terraform, CloudFormation, Pulumi, CDK) - Module structure - State management - Secret injection - Environment variable management
Compile all sections into the template
